Problem_Classification.Algorithm_Purpose: For each input row (prediction vector), count how many other predictions strictly exceed the ground-truth label prediction (or tie and have lower column index). If that count is within top_k, the sample is correct. Accumulate the total correct count.
Problem_Classification.Algorithm_Steps: 1. For each row (sample), thread 0 loads the label index and label prediction value into shared memory. 2. All threads in the block loop over columns (strided by blockDim.x), comparing each prediction to the label prediction. 3. Each thread accumulates a local `ngt` count (number of predictions that beat the label). 4. A CUB BlockReduce sums `ngt` across all threads in the block. 5. Thread 0 checks if the reduced `ngt` <= top_k; if so, increments a local `count`. 6. After all rows are processed, thread 0 atomically adds `count` to the global accuracy counter.
Problem_Classification.Reference_Complexity: Time: O(N * D) — N rows, D columns; each element compared once per row Space: O(1) additional GPU memory beyond input buffers

Bottleneck_Analysis.Arithmetic_Intensity: Each element of Xdata is read once per row pass: ~2 FLOP (comparison + conditional increment) per 4 bytes loaded. Arithmetic intensity ≈ 0.5 FLOP/Byte — far below the RTX 3050's ridge point (~192 GB/s / (peak FP32 ~8 TFLOPS) ≈ 42 FLOP/Byte). The kernel is firmly memory-bound.
Bottleneck_Analysis.Ridge_Point_Comparison: Below theoretical ridge point (0.5 vs ~42 FLOP/Byte)
Bottleneck_Analysis.Dominant_Limiter: Global memory bandwidth — DRAM Throughput ~97% of peak in baseline kernel2

Memory_Access_Profile.Pattern: Streaming — each row of Xdata is read left-to-right, once per sample
Memory_Access_Profile.Read_Write_Ratio: Many-to-1 (N*D reads of Xdata, 1 atomic write to accuracy)
Memory_Access_Profile.Reuse_Factor: 1 — each element read exactly once per kernel invocation
Memory_Access_Profile.Coalescing_Feasibility: Natural — threads access consecutive columns (threadIdx.x + k*blockDim.x), giving coalesced 128-byte transactions across the warp
Memory_Access_Profile.Optimal_Tiling_Hint: Since reuse is 1 and data far exceeds L2 (328 MB vs 1.5 MB L2), tiling into shared memory yields no reuse benefit. The key optimisation is maximising memory-level parallelism (MLP) via loop unrolling and issuing as many outstanding loads as possible. Tile size: not applicable (streaming access). Shared memory: use only for label broadcast (8 bytes per block), as already done in kernel2.

Parallelism_Structure.Granularity: One block processes one row at a time (grid-stride loop over rows); each thread handles ~D/blockDim.x columns per row
Parallelism_Structure.Independence: Independent after reduction — rows are independent; within a row, the ngt partial sums require a BlockReduce barrier
Parallelism_Structure.Synchronization: __syncthreads() after shared-memory label broadcast; CUB BlockReduce (implicit __syncthreads() inside)
Parallelism_Structure.Recommended_Block_Size: 256 threads — matches current code. RTX 3050 has 1536 max threads/SM and 65536 registers/SM. With 27 registers/thread, a block of 256 uses 6912 registers; 6 blocks fit per SM (41472 regs), reaching 1536 threads/SM = 100% theoretical occupancy. Larger blocks do not increase occupancy and increase register pressure.

Data_Shape.Total_Memory_Footprint: Xdata: 8192 * 10000 * 4 = 327,680,000 bytes (~312 MB) labelData: 8192 * 4 = 32,768 bytes accuracy: 4 bytes Total: ~312 MB
